notes: Added the Inca Empire, missing from the 1492 source map.
Added the Aztec Triple Alliance as a state.
Mongolia was the Northern Yuan under Dayan Khan, not the Chagatai Khanate; the Chagatai remnant was Moghulistan.
The Kazakh Khanate (1465) held the eastern steppe; the Great Horde was the last remnant of the Golden Horde.
Greenland was unclaimed between the end of the Norse settlements and Danish recolonisation (1721).
Filled gaps in the source map from the nearest map (within 50 years).
Filled unclaimed land with peoples and cultures from neighbouring maps.
Named the remaining unclaimed regions after their regional peoples.
Java was not Malay sultanates: Majapahit ruled East Java, Madura and Bali until about 1527, and the Hindu Sunda Kingdom West Java until 1579.
The Wattasids and the Zayyanids were sultans, not caliphs.
The Hän people of the Yukon were coloured as the Ming Empire.
North Africa is named for its rulers of the time.
The Nile and the Horn of Africa are named for their peoples and states of the time.
The Caribbean islands were settled from about 5000 BCE (the Bahamas from about 700 CE): Archaic peoples, then the Saladoid peoples and the Taíno.
Peoples who formed in the colonial era are replaced by the peoples who lived there before 1500.
Mesoamerica is named for its peoples and states of the time.
Andean and Amazonian peoples are named for their time.
Hawaii was settled about 1000 CE; before the Hawaiian Kingdom (1795) the islands were separate chiefdoms.
North American cultures are named for their time; the Mississippi and Ohio valleys were the land of the Mississippian and Fort Ancient cultures (boxes approximate).
Modern reservation, treaty and removal-era labels are replaced by the peoples who lived there at the time.
Peoples who reached this land only later are replaced by those who lived there at the time.
